samples.summary: API-key endpoints rerouted through `send()` (401 refresh-and-retry, encoded id) with no test exercising HttpClient
samples.evidence: `listApiKeys`/`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` were rewritten to go through the private `send()` helper, whose documented purpose is that "a refreshable session is never reported as an auth failure just because of which base a call used" (http-client.ts:105-111), plus `encodeURIComponent(id)` on revoke. Nothing tests this: the only HttpClient test in the repo is docs-content.test.ts:301-337 (a single 409 passthrough on getDocContent); grep for `apiKey|refreshSession|refresh` across packages/cli/test finds no refresh-retry test at all. The new command-exit-codes.test.ts replaces the whole client with a Proxy stub (`vi.mock('../src/commands/root.js')`, lines 17-35), so `send()` — including the URL construction and the refresh path it now shares with api-keys — is mocked away entirely.

samples.summary: Vacuous `putCalls` assertion in the new client-side-status import test
samples.evidence: The new test ('exits 1 when create fails with a client-side status', docs-import.test.ts:255-274) builds an inline `ClientCapture` whose `putDocContent: async (_id, doc) => ({ok: true, status: 200, data: doc})` never pushes into `putCalls` (unlike `makeClient` at lines 146-158, which does). `expect(client.putCalls).toEqual([])` at line 273 therefore holds whether or not the PUT was issued — the 'skips PUT' half of the test cannot fail. Only the `exitCode === 1` assertion is real.

samples.summary: New timeout classification (`sawUnboundCallback` → EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR with an 'upgrade the server' message) has no test
samples.evidence: startCallbackServer's timeout branch now picks between a system-error LoginError ('server predates nonce-bound CLI login') and the old user-error timeout depending on `sawUnboundCallback`. packages/cli/test/login.test.ts exercises the 403 rejection paths and `waitForCallback()` resolution but never the timeout branch (no fake timers, no assertion on the two messages/exit codes); nothing in the file references `timed out` or `predates`. The wrapper in `registerLoginCommand` that maps `classifyLoginFailure` to `process.exit` is likewise untested — only `classifyLoginFailure` in isolation is.

samples.summary: The allow branch for `data:` URLs in the new SSRF gate is untested
samples.evidence: `assertFetchableImageUrl` returns early for `url.protocol === 'data:'` (image-fetcher.ts, `if (url.protocol === 'data:') return;`). The CLI's own importer emits data: URLs (`inlineBase64Uploader`, docs-import.test.ts:55-75), so blocking them would be a real regression, but image-fetcher.test.ts only tests blocked schemes (`file:`, `blob:`) and never drives `createImageFetcher` with a `data:` src. Similarly `.local`/`.localhost` suffixes in `isInternalHostname` are unexercised (only `localhost` and `metadata.google.internal` appear).
searchedFor: read the createImageFetcher SSRF gate describe block in the diff

samples.summary: Export test title claims 'without writing the file' but never asserts it
samples.evidence: `it('exits 2 on a 401 without writing the file', ...)` (command-exit-codes.test.ts:113-117) asserts only `process.exitCode === 2`; no fs spy or existence check backs the 'without writing the file' claim. Harmless, but the title over-states coverage.

samples.summary: Controller's no-nonce fallback and nonce URL-encoding are untested
samples.evidence: The new redirect builds `nonceParam` conditionally on `state.nonce` and runs it through `encodeURIComponent`. The added controller test (auth.controller.spec.ts, 'echoes the CLI nonce…') uses `'nonce-abc'`, which needs no escaping, and there is no test for a state without a nonce (empty `nonceParam`). cli-auth.store.spec.ts was not extended for the nonce round trip either (its `toEqual({csrf, mode, port})` at line 35 passes because `nonce: undefined` is ignored by toEqual).
searchedFor: read the auth.controller.spec.ts hunk in the diff

finding.summary: API-key endpoints rerouted through `send()` (401 refresh-and-retry, encoded id) with no test exercising HttpClient
finding.evidence: `listApiKeys`/`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` were rewritten to go through the private `send()` helper, whose documented purpose is that "a refreshable session is never reported as an auth failure just because of which base a call used" (http-client.ts:105-111), plus `encodeURIComponent(id)` on revoke. Nothing tests this: the only HttpClient test in the repo is docs-content.test.ts:301-337 (a single 409 passthrough on getDocContent); grep for `apiKey|refreshSession|refresh` across packages/cli/test finds no refresh-retry test at all. The new command-exit-codes.test.ts replaces the whole client with a Proxy stub (`vi.mock('../src/commands/root.js')`, lines 17-35), so `send()` — including the URL construction and the refresh path it now shares with api-keys — is mocked away entirely.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: the API-key methods (http-client.ts:263-271) now go through the private send() helper, which owns the 401 refresh-and-retry (http-client.ts:112-156, refreshSession 59-95) and builds an absolute URL from apiKeysBase (259-262) plus encodeURIComponent(id) on revoke. No test exercises any of it. The only test that constructs a real HttpClient is docs-content.test.ts:306-336, which stubs fetch with one 409 and calls getDocContent — it covers only the non-401 pass-through, never the api-keys base, the refresh branch, or the id encoding. command-exit-codes.test.ts:17-35 replaces getClient with a Proxy that returns a canned object, so its api-keys case (158-162) never reaches HttpClient. namespaces.test.ts:50-53 and schema.test.ts:32-34,82-85 assert only command/schema registration. Repo-wide greps for `new HttpClient|getClient(`, `apiKeysBase|encodeURIComponent(id)`, and `auth/refresh|SESSION_EXPIRED` surfaced no other CLI-client test; packages/backend/test/api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts drives the Nest controller via supertest and does not touch the CLI client, and there are no *.test.ts files under packages/cli/src nor any e2e/integration dir invoking the CLI. Changed behavior with no meaningful test = major under the test-adequacy rubric.
